summary: 134-item partial extraction: resolves the abstract finite-type fibre-dimension argument and compatible perfect-scheme transfer, supplies both Frobenius endpoint squares, reuses two further pinned dimension lemmas, and replaces an impossible original-lattice lifting obligation by an explicit twisted A2 counterexample and adjoint-descent boundary. items.statement: For a surjective finite-type morphism X→Y of nonempty finite-type schemes over a field, if every geometric fiber has dimension at least d, then dim X≥dim Y+d. Apply to bounded models, and pass through perfection by a proved dimension comparison.

proofOutline: Replace Y by a reduced irreducible component Z of maximal dimension, and X by X×_Y Z; its dimension is at most dim X. Let η be the generic point of Z.

items.name: Support survives the Demazure construction
items.statement: supp_σ(a) contains supp_σ(η_σ(w)), because support of * is a union and supp(x′y′(y′)⁻¹z)⊂supp(x′y′)∪supp((y′)⁻¹z).

items.name: Second dimension gain and final identification
items.statement: With the same estimate, dim X_3 ≥ dim X_5 + ℓ(η_σ(w)) − ℓ(a). The length-additive map gives X_5 ≅ X_{σ(at^γ)}(b), universally homeomorphic to X_{at^γ}(b).

items.name: Nonemptiness and virtual-dimension comparison
items.statement: If X_{at^γ}(b)≠∅, the two surjective correspondences imply X_w(b)≠∅ and dim X_w(b)−dim X_{at^γ}(b)≥(ℓw−ℓ(at^γ)+ℓη_σ(w)−ℓa)/2=d_w(b)−d_{at^γ}(b).
proofOutline: Add the two gains and cancel the common defect/Newton terms in the virtual dimensions.

items.name: Reduction to a cordial element
items.statement: In the working full-coweight realization of the simple quasi-split datum, for a shrunken w there exist dominant γ≥_Zλ_w^{♭♭} and a∈W0 with supp_σ(a)⊃supp_σ(η_σ(w)) such that w⇒_σa t^γ. This is the adjoint-carrier form used by the proof. For a different original cocharacter lattice, transfer the final theorem via /61; requiring the same γ in that lattice can be false.
items.note: Corrected carrier qualification for the printed Theorem5.5, recorded under E6. In ²A2 with actual lattice Q∨ and λbb=(1,3), no actual γ can satisfy γ≥_Zλbb. This is not a counterexample to the final geometric Theorem6.1 after a valid adjoint reduction.
proofOutline: Collect the constructed γ bound, full-support propagation and /83; this remains gated by /61 and /69.

items.name: Levi Kottwitz obstruction
items.statement: If w is a (J,v,σ)-alcove element and κ_{M_J}(v⁻¹wσ(v)) differs from κ_{M_J}(b′) for every b′∈[b]∩M_J(L), then X_w(b)=∅. No basic assumption is needed on b.

items.note: GHN15 §3 is stated for tamely ramified quasi-split semisimple groups. Its contraction proof gives this direction without basic b; removing its tame geometry hypotheses still needs justification. Do not import the false nonbasic uniqueness assertion corrected in the erratum.
proofOutline: Use the P-alcove contraction/Hodge–Newton argument for each Levi representative; never invoke the false nonbasic uniqueness statement.

items.name: Corrected conjugating element for the support obstruction
items.statement: Write w=x t^λy as in §2.2 and put J=supp_σ(σ⁻¹(y)x). GHN15 Lemma3.6.3 makes w a (J,x,σ)-alcove element, and x⁻¹wσ(x)=t^λ yσ(x)=t^λσ(η_σ(w)) belongs to Wtilde_J.
items.note: The printed (J,σ⁻¹(y),σ) and later conjugate use inconsistent inverse conventions. Using the original normal-form left factor x matches the cited lemma and leaves the translation λ unchanged. This is a repair of the proof’s notation, not a change to the theorem.
proofOutline: The printed (J,σ⁻¹(y),σ) and later conjugate use inconsistent inverse conventions. Using the original normal-form left factor x matches the cited lemma and leaves the translation λ unchanged. This is a repair of the proof’s notation, not a change to the theorem.

items.name: Newton vector and Levi Kottwitz comparison
items.statement: For b′∈[b]∩M_J(L), its M_J-dominant ν^M_b′ lies in W0ν_b, and ν_b−ν^M_b′ is a nonnegative rational sum of simple coroots. If its Levi κ equals that of t^λσ(η), then λ^♦−ν^M_b′ lies in the rational span of J-coroots.
items.note: Keep every b′ rather than assuming [b]∩M_J(L) is a single Levi class; the latter requires basic b.
proofOutline: Compare the Levi Newton point with its G-dominant representative; apply the Levi Kottwitz map and σ-average before passing to the J-coroot span.

items.name: Emptiness for proper σ-support
items.statement: For w shrunken and λ_w^♦−ν_b having strictly positive coefficient on every simple coroot, if supp_σ(η_σ(w)) is proper then X_w(b)=∅.
items.note: The strict cone cannot lie in the span of a proper σ-stable J after adding ν_b−ν^M_b′. This uses the strict Newton assumption of Thm6.1 even though the first line of §6.2 only repeats the double-flat assumption.
proofOutline: Strict positivity on every simple coroot cannot fit in a proper J-span after adding ν_b−ν_b′^M; apply /86.

items.name: Basic class below a fixed Kottwitz fibre
items.statement: For κ=κ(w), choose τ∈Ω representing the basic class with that κ. If κ(b)=κ, then [τdot]≤[b].
items.note: Uniqueness is for the σ-class/basic class, not a unique element τ of Ω.
proofOutline: Use the basic classification and minimality in a fixed κ-fibre from BG1; τ itself need not be uniquely chosen.

items.name: Kottwitz preservation in the working full-coweight datum
items.statement: In the full-coweight datum P∨, the constructed dominant γ satisfies κ_P(t^γ)=κ_P(w) in (P∨/Q∨)_σ: β−λ is a coroot term plus (σ⁻¹−1)ρ∨_J, and γ−β is a coroot term. No equality κ_G(t^γ)=κ_G(w) is asserted when γ is not a cocharacter of G.
items.note: The ²A2 example in /127 has γ∉Q∨. Equality in auxiliary σ-coinvariants cannot be inverted to manufacture an original-group translation. /61 transfers final geometric conclusions instead.
proofOutline: Apply the explicit coroot-plus-coboundary calculation of /127 in P∨, the lattice actually used by the construction.
Finite Weyl factors have zero Kottwitz class; passing β to γ adds a coroot.
Retain G1 only for the original-group geometric use, not for this elementary auxiliary κ computation.

items.name: Basic nonemptiness used for the reduced element
items.statement: For the actual dominant γ and full-σ-support a constructed in He21 Theorem5.5, with κ(τ)=κ(t^γ), the main proof needs X_(at^γ)(τdot)≠∅. In the nonzero-γ equal-characteristic simple-adjoint source scope, /120 supplies a non-shrunken seed; /121 is the zero branch. General-scope transport is the explicit remaining obligation /122.
items.note: G3 — now routed: the construction need not produce a shrunken a t^γ. In split adjoint A2 take λ=ω2∨=(0,1), y=1, x=s2s1. Then J=∅, J′={s1}, x′=s2, z=s1, γ=λ, y′=1 and a=s1*s2=s1s2. On the base alcove with u<0,v<0,u+v>−1, w maps (u,v) to (v−1,1−u−v), outside every critical strip; a t^γ maps it to (1−u−v,u), whose second coordinate is in (−1,0). Both finite parts have full support. Thus He15 Thm2.27 cannot directly be applied to this constructed a t^γ. Supply a more general basic-seed theorem or alter the reduction; this does not disprove the main theorem. The earlier A1 suspicion was rejected after checking the exact sign convention. Follow-up: He14 Proposition11.6 with J=S and Proposition11.7, combined with its Corollary6.2, supply the restricted replacement /118–120 without any shrunken premise. Do not use He14 Theorem11.4, which would reintroduce that premise; retain the /117 source corrections and /122 transfer frontier.
proofOutline: Split γ≠0 and γ=0. Use /120 and /121 in their source scope, then the still-open /122 for the full He21 setting.

items.name: Lower dimension bound by cordial saturation
items.statement: Assume the main hypotheses, the reduction w⇒a t^γ and its basic nonemptiness input. Then γ^♦≥(λ_w^{♭♭})^♦≥ν_b and equal κ give [τ]≤[b]≤[t^γ]. Cordial saturation makes X_{at^γ}(b) nonempty with dimension d_{at^γ}(b), hence dim X_w(b)≥d_w(b).
proofOutline: Place the basic lower endpoint and b below [t^γ] with equal κ, apply cordial saturation/dimension, and transfer through w⇒at^γ.

items.name: Main nonemptiness criterion
items.statement: Under the paper’s standing simple quasi-split G/F hypothesis, let b∈G(L), w∈Wtilde with w a shrunken, λ_w^♦−ν_b∈Σ_{α∈Δ}Q_{>0}α∨ and (λ_w^{♭♭})^♦≥ν_b. Then X_w(b)≠∅ iff κ(b)=κ(w) and supp_σ(η_σ(w))=S. Here λbb is defined in the explicitly specified full-coweight rational apartment, and the original-group assertion requires the adjoint descent in G1.
items.note: Both Newton hypotheses are retained; no claim is made for all w or for all [b] ≤ [ṫ^λ] (see gap G11 and Remark 6.2). The statement is the one the paper proves, in the adjoint datum of /61, from which G1 records the descent a design job must plan.
proofOutline: Combine the Kottwitz obstruction, proper-support emptiness and /93's construction of a nonempty locus.

items.name: Main dimension formula
items.statement: With all hypotheses of the preceding main criterion and its two nonemptiness conditions, dim X_w(b)=(ℓw+ℓη_σ(w)−def_G(b))/2−〈ν_b,ρ〉.
proofOutline: Match /93's lower bound against the virtual upper bound /21.

items.name: Minuscule exception in the two Newton bounds
items.statement: If G is split and λ_w is minuscule, then λ_w^{♭♭}=λ_w; therefore the weak double-flat bound alone does not imply strict positivity of λ_w^♦−ν_b.
items.note: A nonzero dominant difference in an irreducible root system lies in the strictly positive rational simple-coroot cone, but zero is a necessary exception.
proofOutline: Check the minuscule subtraction case in the actual lattice; equality λ^{♭♭}=λ allows the strict difference to vanish.

items.name: Basic-class double-flat bound
items.statement: For basic [b] with κ(b)=κ(w), (λ_w^{♭♭})^♦≥ν_b in the setup where the double-flat carrier/Kottwitz compatibility is established.
proofOutline: Use dominance of the double-flat vector and the basic minimum in the same correctly compared κ-fibre.

items.name: Two-rho sufficient Newton bound
items.statement: If λ_w^♦≥ν_b+2ρ∨, then (λ_w^{♭♭})^♦≥ν_b and λ_w^♦−ν_b is strictly positive on all simple-coroot coefficients. The argument uses 2ρ∨−ρ∨_J−η∨_J≥0 in the rational coroot cone.
items.note: λ_w−2ρ∨ itself need not be dominant; only its σ-average is constrained.
proofOutline: Bound ρ∨_J+η∨_J by 2ρ∨ in the rational coroot cone, average under σ, and retain strict positivity of 2ρ∨.

items.name: Effective-region nonemptiness criterion
items.statement: For G simple quasi-split, w a shrunken and λ_w^♦≥ν_b+2ρ∨, X_w(b)≠∅ iff κ(b)=κ(w) and supp_σ(η_σ(w))=S.
proofOutline: Apply /94 after /98; the shrunken condition remains a separate input.

items.name: Effective-region dimension formula
items.statement: Under the preceding Cor.6.4 hypotheses and nonemptiness, dim X_w(b)=d_w(b).
proofOutline: Apply /95 with /98 and the established nonemptiness conditions.

items.name: Sufficiently large fundamental ray
items.statement: For an irreducible root system and fixed b, if λ_w=nω∨ is an allowed integral multiple of a fundamental coweight and n is sufficiently large, then λ_w^♦≥ν_b+2ρ∨.
items.note: Only multiples lying in the actual cocharacter lattice are allowed. This supplies the Newton bound, not the separate shrunken-alcove assumption.
proofOutline: In an irreducible root system each fundamental coweight has positive rational simple-coroot coordinates; large allowed integral multiples dominate the fixed bound.

items.name: Necessary Hodge–Newton conditions
items.statement: If X_w(b)≠∅, then κ(b)=κ(w) and ν_b≤λ_w^♦.
proofOutline: The Iwahori double coset is contained in the appropriate special-parahoric double coset; apply /48 and κ necessity.

items.name: Levi reduction for proper support
items.statement: For w in a shrunken chamber with proper J=supp_σ(η_σ(w)), use the appropriate (J,v,σ)-alcove and Hodge–Newton decomposition to reduce the ADLV to suitable Levi ADLV data; recheck Theorem6.1’s hypotheses on each simple Levi factor before applying it.
items.note: The side remark is not a theorem that all classes satisfying Mazur’s inequality are covered, nor an unrestricted equality of G- and Levi-varieties without the required quotient/components. GHKR10 Thm2.1.4 and GHN15 Thm3.3.1 require separate decomposition.
proofOutline: Construct the actual Levi comparison with its components/quotients from GHKR/GHN, then recheck the simple-factor hypotheses. This is not a blanket consequence of Mazur's inequality.

items.name: Corrected adjoint comparison on connected components
items.statement: In equal characteristic with char(k) not dividing |π1(G_ad)|, G→G_ad identifies each selected connected component of its affine flag variety with the corresponding component for G_ad; a global immersion requires injectivity of the map on component groups. The induced componentwise ADLV comparison is GHN15 Cor.2.2.2.
items.note: The erratum explicitly removes the automatic injectivity claim. In mixed characteristic the cited original passage only establishes a set-theoretic comparison; dimension requires the later perfect-geometry bridge.
proofOutline: Use the corrected GHN componentwise flag isomorphism and check the ADLV graph condition on the selected components. A global immersion requires an additional injectivity hypothesis.

items.name: Levi class uniqueness only for a basic G-class
items.statement: If [b] is basic and J is σ-stable, [b]∩M_J(L) contains at most one σ-conjugacy class of M_J(L). This statement is false without basic b.
items.locator: GHN15 erratum Proposition0.0.2; He21 Thm6.3 footnote
items.note: Counterexample GL2 with diagonal Levi: diag(t,1),diag(1,t) are G-σ-conjugate but not torus-σ-conjugate.
proofOutline: For a basic G-class the Newton vector is central and equals its dominant representative; apply the Levi classification. The nonbasic diagonal GL2 example is the regression guard.

items.name: Generic equal-parameter extended affine Hecke algebra
items.statement: For a based reduced root datum with extended affine Weyl group Wtilde=Wa⋊Ω, construct the free A=Z[v,v⁻¹]-module with basis T_w and associative multiplication T_xT_y=T_xy when lengths add and T_s²=1+(v−v⁻¹)T_s for affine simple s. A finite-order based automorphism δ acts by T_w↦T_δ(w).
proofOutline: Construct multiplication using reduced words, prove braid-independence and associativity, and extend by the Ω-action; these are construction obligations, not assumed structure fields.
Keep this generic deformation distinct from the pinned double-coset Hecke ring. Compare specializations with SR.1 only under an actual Iwahori–Matsumoto theorem.

items.name: Finite Coxeter part has zero Newton vector
items.statement: In the semisimple full-coweight affine datum, if c is δ-Coxeter in W0 then cδ is elliptic on P∨⊗Q. Thus 1−cδ is invertible and every t^μ cδ is conjugate by a rational translation to cδ, has finite order, and has Newton vector zero.

items.name: Minimal elements of a finite-Coxeter-part class
items.statement: For an irreducible reduced root system, Wtilde=P∨⋊W0, and a finite-order based automorphism δ, a Wa-conjugacy class in Wtilde⋊〈δ〉 with finite Coxeter part has a unique maximal proper τ-stable affine-simple subset J whose twisted Coxeter elements in W_Jτ are exactly its minimal-length elements. Every element of that class reduces by non-increasing simple conjugations to each minimal element; τ is its length-zero component.

Combine those representatives with the HN reduction/nice-class theorem. The case list has been read, but its exceptional-type computations and the HN theorem remain proof-decomposition frontiers.
Do not claim the unique J is literally the ordinary support of one twisted Coxeter word: for nontrivial twisting, J is its τ-saturated support.

Then some δ-Coxeter c∈W0 satisfies T_(xt^μy)−h^(ℓx+ℓy−ℓc)T_(t^μc)∈H_+ + C_δ. There is no shrunken-alcove hypothesis.
proofOutline: Induct on |J| and then ℓx. Let J1={i∈J:t^μys_i is not left minimal}; show it is proper in the nonempty-J induction case.
Decompose x=u x1 with x1 left-minimal for W_(δ⁻¹J1), and put x′=x1*δ(u). If x1≠1, any selected left descent i lies in J\δ⁻¹J1. This corrects the printed membership sign (confirmed in the page image).

If x∈W_(δ⁻¹J1), repeat twisted rotation on δ^n(x); full saturated support contradicts containment in the proper subset. The complete corrected twisted induction is a remaining proof-verification task, not a formalized result.

items.name: Local finite-type form of the fibre-dimension estimate
items.statement: Let f:X→Y be a surjective finite-type morphism of schemes locally of finite type over an algebraically closed field, with finite dim Y and every geometric fibre of dimension at least d≥0. Then dim X≥dim Y+d. It suffices to restrict to a nonempty finite-type open piece of a maximal-dimensional irreducible component of Y.

proofOutline: Choose a reduced maximal-dimensional component Z of Y. Since Y is locally noetherian and finite dimensional, Z has a nonempty affine open U of finite type over k and dim U=dim Z.
The base change X×_Y U is finite type over k, so apply /68; it is locally closed in X and has dimension at most dim X.
Only a finite-type neighbourhood of one target component is needed; no global quasi-compactness or global finiteness of the component set is asserted.

In He21 §5.4 set r=(y′)⁻¹z, u=t^{ρ∨_J}y, v=σ(w1), q0=uv=σ(x′y′t^γ), h=σ(x′y′), k=σ(t^γ). Then X2≅X3×_{O_q0}C(u,v;q0), using e23(g1,g3)=(g3,bσ(g1)); and X4≅X5×_{O_σ(a)}C(r,h;σ(a)), using e45(g1,g4)=(g1,g4). These equalities are functorial identities of relative-position moduli, before deperfection. Conditional on /123, their local finite-type or pfp hypotheses follow by base change.

proofOutline: In the first square, a point of X3 has pos(g1,g3)=r and pos(g3,bσ(g1))=q0. Pulling back C inserts exactly g2 with pos(g3,g2)=u and pos(g2,bσ(g1))=v, the defining data of X2. This works over every test algebra, not just geometric points.
Use ℓ(q0)=ℓ(h)+ℓ(k) to identify X3 with the expanded triple (g1,g3,g4), as in He21 p.11.
In the second square, X5 has pos(g1,g4)=σ(a) and pos(g4,bσ(g1))=k. Pulling back inserts exactly g3 with positions r,h, the defining data of X4.

The first q0 is the ordinary product uv; the second σ(a)=r*h is the Demazure product. Apply respectively /66 and /67 for the geometric-fibre bounds; apply /124 or /126 after /123 supplies the local model.

items.name: Compatible perfection models transfer fibre dimension bounds

By /133, |X|≅|X0|, |Y|≅|Y0|, and geometric fibres are compatible perfections. If f is surjective and every geometric fibre has dimension at least d, then f0 satisfies the same conditions and dim X≥dim Y+d by /68. For algebraic spaces, first supply the corresponding dimension theorem for spaces or a justified étale reduction; the scheme theorem alone is not enough.
proofOutline: Use /134 to deperfect the actual morphism after a Frobenius twist of a source model.
Use /133 for the geometric-fibre cartesian square and dimension preservation; surjectivity is a statement about the same underlying spaces.

items.name: Lattice comparison for the auxiliary construction
items.statement: For an unramified semisimple root datum with σ-stable Q∨⊂Λ⊂P∨, the inclusion Λ→P∨ is W0- and σ-equivariant and preserves root pairings, dominant representatives of points of Λ, affine length, and integral-coroot comparisons between points of Λ. The He21 auxiliary construction is carried out in P∨. For its β=λ−ρ∨_J+(x′)⁻¹σ⁻¹ρ∨_J and γ=dom(β), one has [γ]=[λ] in (P∨/Q∨)_σ. This does not imply β, γ or λbb belong to Λ; actual-lattice Kottwitz equality is meaningful only after the needed integral comparison. General ramified data, inertia torsion and reduced-root adapters remain G1.
proofOutline: A simple reflection changes an integral coweight by an integral multiple of a coroot. Consequently Weyl translates preserve both Λ and its coroot cosets; σ-equivariance and dominance follow from the pinned root datum.
Compute β−λ=((x′)⁻¹σ⁻¹ρ∨_J−σ⁻¹ρ∨_J)+(σ⁻¹ρ∨_J−ρ∨_J). The first term lies in Q∨ and the second vanishes in σ-coinvariants of P∨/Q∨. Passing to the dominant representative changes by another coroot.
In a genuinely split datum σ=1, β−λ is a coroot, hence γ lies in Λ. This conclusion does not extend to a nontrivial diagram action.

The explicit ²A2 computation in the note disproves original-lattice lifting in general. Transfer the final nonemptiness/dimension conclusions through adjoint comparison /61 instead of requiring a nonexistent lift of the intermediate γ.
items.note: Supporting computation for finding E6, in unramified simply connected quasi-split type ²A_2, in fundamental-coweight coordinates: P^∨ = Z², Q^∨ = {(a,b); a + 2b ≡ 0 mod 3}, σ(a,b) = (b,a); λ = (3,3) ∈ Q^∨, x = 1, y = s_1 give J = {s_1}, J′ = ∅, x′ = s_2, z = 1, ρ^∨_J = η^∨_J = (1,0), λ^♭♭ = (1,3), γ = (3,2), y′ = 1 and a = s_2, and the root intervals of w = t^λ s_1 on the base alcove are (−3,−2), (−4,−3), (−7,−6), so w is shrunken. items.name: Affine dimension is invariant under a field extension
items.statement: Let k⊂K be fields and A a finitely generated commutative k-algebra, allowing the zero algebra. Then dim(K⊗_k A)=dim A. This is the affine ingredient for geometric-fibre dimension invariance; it is not by itself a theorem about arbitrary schemes.

items.name: Finite dimension of a nonzero finite-type algebra
items.statement: For a field k and a nonzero finitely generated commutative k-algebra A, dim A is finite.
items.note: Pinned statement and proof read. Nontriviality is explicit; do not apply this class to the zero algebra.

items.name: Generic fibre dimension from transcendence degree
items.statement: Let f:V→Z be dominant between nonempty integral schemes of finite type over a field k, and η the generic point of Z. Then dim(V_η)=trdeg_{k(Z)}k(V)=dim V−dim Z. The same equality holds for a nonempty affine open in V that meets the generic fibre.

proofOutline: On compatible affine opens, pass from an injective map of finite-type domains A→B to Frac(A)⊗_A B. Its fraction field is Frac(B).
Apply the dimension/transcendence-degree equality (Stacks 00P0) to A, B and the generic-fibre algebra, and the tower formula for transcendence degree.
Dimensions of nonempty affine opens in an integral finite-type k-scheme agree by the same function-field computation; field extension preserves fibre dimension by /130.

items.name: Perfection preserves fibre products and underlying dimensions
items.statement: Over a perfect field k of characteristic p>0, the perfection functor on algebraic spaces is right adjoint to inclusion of perfect spaces, and ε_X:X^perf→X is a universal homeomorphism. Consequently perfection preserves fibre products. For a map X0→Y0 and a geometric point Spec Ω→Y0 with Ω algebraically closed, (X0×_Y0 Spec Ω)^perf identifies with X0^perf×_Y0^perf Spec Ω. Their topological dimensions agree.
items.locator: Zhu17 Appendix A.1.2, Corollary A.3 and Remark A.4, printed pp.465–466
items.note: Selected source proof read; statement includes actual functorial fibre compatibility, not only separate homeomorphisms.
proofOutline: Construct X^perf as the inverse limit of Frobenius, using the étale-local affine construction and relative Frobenius for étale maps.
The right-adjoint universal property preserves fibre products; Ω is already perfect.
The projection from perfection is a universal homeomorphism, hence identifies the specialisation posets and their chain dimensions.

items.name: A morphism of pfp perfect spaces has a compatible model
items.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p>0 and f:X→Y a morphism between perfect algebraic spaces perfectly of finite presentation over k. There are finite-presentation algebraic spaces X0,Y0 and f0:X0→Y0 with f=f0^perf. If X and Y are schemes, scheme models can be used.
items.locator: Zhu17 Proposition A.17 and proof, printed pp.472–473; Proposition A.15 and Remark A.4
items.note: Read with its proof. Choose a model of the target, then adjust the Frobenius twist of a source model; independent deperfections are insufficient.
proofOutline: Choose finite-presentation models using A.15; if the original perfect objects are schemes, their models are schemes by Remark A.4.
Compose f with Y→Y0. Finite-presentation limit descent factors this map through a sufficiently high Frobenius twist of X0.
Rename that twist as X0. Its perfection is X, and the descended morphism has perfection f by the right-adjoint property.

gaps.detail: The reduction that §5 needs is to adjoint groups, and the paper's summary of it omits that word (finding E6): ρ^∨_J is a coweight of G, and so w_1, w_2 and a t^γ are elements of W̃, exactly when X_*(T)_{Γ_0} is the full coweight lattice. A design job therefore plans §§5.2–5.4 in the adjoint datum, and must plan two things the paper does not write out: the descent of Theorem 6.1's conclusion from G_ad back to G — a comparison of κ, of the Newton point, of the defect and of the rational inequality (λ^♭♭_w)^♦ ≥ ν_b, component by component — and the cost of the cited reduction, which holds under char k ∤ |π_1(G_ad)| and, after the authors' erratum (finding E13), only component by component. It must not plan a lift of γ, λ^♭♭_w, w_1 or w_2 to a smaller lattice: item /127 shows in unramified ²A_2 that no such lift exists, and none is needed.

§5.4 deduces dim X_2 ≥ dim X_3 + N_1 from a lower bound on every fibre of π: X_2 → X_3, using [GW10, Corollary 14.116] on an irreducible component Z of X_3. The inference itself is sound — the generic point of Z lies outside every proper closed subset Z_Y, whatever the number of irreducible components Y of π^{-1}(Z) — but two things a formalisation needs are left implicit and a design job must plan them: which category the objects live in (in equal characteristic X_w(b) is the F̄_q-points of a scheme; in mixed characteristic the carrier is a perfect scheme, by [BS17] and Zhu's appendix, see finding E8), and a fibre-dimension theorem valid there, since the affine flag variety is an ind-scheme and X_w(b) is not quasi-compact. Items /68 and /124 give the generic-point form of the estimate for finite-type morphisms, /123 and /125 the bounded convolution models the two maps of §5.4 require, and /126 with /133 and /134 the transfer through perfection.

The basic seed X_{a t^γ}(τ̇) ≠ ∅ of §6.3 is quoted from the shrunken criterion [He15, Theorem 2.27], whose hypothesis the constructed a t^γ does not satisfy whenever γ is not regular (finding E1). A design job plans the seed from the criterion that holds for every element — [GHN15, Theorem A], that is Corollary 3.6.1 together with Theorem 4.4.7 — or from the class-polynomial route of [He14, §11.2] with Corollary 6.2, which items /117–/120 record, with /121 for γ = 0. It must not plan it from [He14, Theorem 11.4] or [GHN15, Theorem B], both of which assume a shrunken alcove.

The minimal length theory is imported, not proved here: He–Nie's reduction of a σ-conjugacy class to its minimal length elements (Theorem 3.1), the cocenter of the extended affine Hecke algebra with its basis of minimal classes and the class polynomials (items /106–/110), the 'dimension = degree' theorem and the geometry of straight and fundamental elements behind Theorem 3.2, and He–Yang's determination of the minimal elements of a class with finite Coxeter part (items /114–/116). A design job imports these from the stages named in the routes and plans only what the paper adds.

Cordiality is taken from Milićević–Viehmann: the generic Newton point [b_w] of an Iwahori double coset, the saturation property and the dimension formula for cordial elements (Theorem 4.1, items /41–/45). Their proofs — the purity and the local geometry of the Newton stratification they rest on — are not planned here. §4.1 also records that fully characterising cordial elements is difficult, and §4.4 that not every x t^λ is ≈_σ-equivalent to an element of the dominant chamber, so a design job must not plan a classification of cordial elements nor treat the two families of §4.2 and §4.4 as one.

The step in §4.3 that passes from the Iwahori double coset to its closure — [Vi14, Corollary 5.6], that the maximal σ-conjugacy class meeting Ĭ ẇ Ĭ is the one meeting its closure (item /49) — is quoted; Viehmann's proof and the hypotheses it needs are not planned here. The citation was added when the paper was revised: the arXiv version asserts only the inclusion Ĭ ẇ_S ṫ^λ Ĭ ⊂ K̆ ṫ^λ K̆.

Mazur's inequality in both forms is quoted: the upper bound dim X_w(b) ≤ d_w(b) (Theorem 2.1, from [He14, Corollary 10.4] for residually split groups and [He15, Theorem 2.30] in general) and the nonemptiness criterion in the affine Grassmannian (Theorem 4.4, from [Ga10] for unramified groups and [He14, Theorem 7.1] in general). A design job imports them; the paper proves neither, and the ramified and mixed-characteristic transfer of the second is part of what it imports.

The P-alcove machinery is imported from [GHKR10] and [GHN15]: the (J,x,σ)-alcove elements, the Kottwitz obstruction (Theorem 6.3 = [GHN15, Corollary 3.6.1]), the lemma that makes w an alcove element (Lemma 3.6.3, whose data the paper misquotes — finding E2), and the Hodge–Newton decomposition quoted in §6.5 for the case supp_σ(η_σ(w)) ⊊ S. Two of the propositions behind them are corrected by the authors' erratum (findings E13 and E14), and §6.5 does not make the resulting Levi affine Deligne–Lusztig variety explicit, so a design job must plan the reduction it names rather than assume it.

The rank-one and finite-level geometry behind the Deligne–Lusztig reduction (Proposition 3.3, items /128–/129) and the finite Deligne–Lusztig variety in the reductive quotient of a special parahoric used for the γ = 0 seed (item /121) are quoted from [DL76], [GH10] and [He14, §4]; Lang's theorem and the comparison of relative positions in the quotient are not planned here.

A layer of small combinatorial facts is used throughout and is not proved in the paper: the Demazure product with its associativity and monotonicity (He09, items /37–/40), minimal coset representatives and the length identities of §5.4, the dominance and integral coroot orders with the finiteness of dominant coweights below a given one, the normalised subtraction of §5.1, and the sign facts about shrunken chambers taken from [GH10, §2.3 and Lemma 2.6.1]. A design job takes these from the root-system roadmap this extraction extends, and plans only the ones that roadmap does not have.

What the paper leaves open, in its own words, and which a design job must therefore not plan as part of it. For [b] basic and w outside the shrunken Weyl chamber, §1.3 records that no conjectural dimension formula has even been formulated, while the nonemptiness pattern there is known ([GHN15]); for other nonbasic classes outside the hypotheses of Theorem 6.1, §1.3 records that little is known. The hypotheses of Theorem 6.1 are not removable by the method: Remark 6.2 shows that λ^♭♭_w = λ_w when G is split and λ_w is minuscule, which is why λ^♦_w − ν_b ∈ Σ_{α∈Δ}Q_{>0}α^∨ is assumed, and §6.4 gives λ^♦_w ≥ ν_b + 2ρ^∨ as the simple sufficient condition (Corollary 6.4). The paper also does not determine the nonemptiness pattern for the classes [b] with κ(b) = κ(w) and ν_b ≤ λ^♦_w that fall outside those hypotheses, and the application announced in §1.2 — a dimension formula for the group-theoretic analogue of Newton strata for sufficiently large dominant coweights — is joint work with Q. Yu ([HY21]), not proved here.

sourceIssues.locator: §6.3, p. 14 (published version; the same sentence is in arXiv:2001.03325)
sourceIssues.printed: By [He15, Theorem 2.27], X_{at^γ}(τ̇) ≠ ∅, where τ ∈ Ω with κ(w) = κ(t^γ) = κ(τ).
sourceIssues.correction: The basic seed has to be taken from a criterion that does not assume a shrunken alcove — [GHN15, Theorem A] (Corollary 3.6.1 with Theorem 4.4.7), which is stated for every element of W̃ — or proved for a t^γ directly; [He15, Theorem 2.27] cannot be quoted as printed.
sourceIssues.reason: The cited theorem reads (arXiv:1511.01386, Theorem 2.27, the numbering of the published survey, cross-checked through its Theorems 2.28, 2.30 and 2.34, which this paper cites for the results they carry): 'Assume that G is simple. Let w ∈ W̃ such that wσ(a) is contained in a Shrunken Weyl chamber. Then for any basic σ-conjugacy class [b], Ĭ ẇ Ĭ ∩ [b] ≠ ∅ if and only if κ(w) = κ(b) and η_σ(w) is not contained in W_M for any proper standard ς-stable Levi M.' The element it is applied to is the a t^γ produced by Theorem 5.5, and that element is not shrunken whenever γ is not regular: if ⟨γ, α⟩ = 0 for a root α, then every point v of the alcove a t^γ(a) satisfies ⟨v, a(α)⟩ = ⟨u, α⟩ for a point u of the base alcove, so 0 < |⟨v, a(α)⟩| < 1 and v lies in the critical strip of ±a(α). Non-regular γ is the normal case, not an edge case: the proof of Theorem 5.5 introduces K = {s ∈ S; s(γ) = γ} and y′ ∈ W_0^K for exactly this reason, and §6.4 discusses λ_w = nω^∨ for a fundamental coweight ω^∨, where γ lies on the walls. A worked instance in split adjoint type A_2: λ = ω_2^∨, y = 1, x = s_2s_1 give J = ∅, J′ = {s_1}, x′ = s_2, z = s_1, γ = λ, y′ = 1 and a = s_1 ∗ s_2 = s_1s_2; on the base alcove {u < 0, v < 0, u + v > −1} the element w = x t^λ y is outside every critical strip, while a t^γ sends (u,v) to (1−u−v, u), whose second coordinate lies in (−1,0), so a t^γ is not shrunken although both finite parts have full support. The conclusion is not contradicted — [GHN15, Theorem A] is available for every w — but the step as written applies its source outside its hypothesis.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 5.1 with its proof, p. 8 (both versions)
sourceIssues.printed: Then the set {μ'; μ' is dominant, μ' + λ' ≥_Z λ} contains a unique minimal element with respect the dominance order ≥_Z. … [proof] The statement is proved.
sourceIssues.correction: Two steps have to be added: that the set is nonempty, and that it has a minimal element at all.
sourceIssues.reason: What the printed proof establishes is that the set is lower directed: for any two of its elements μ'_1, μ'_2 it produces a dominant μ in the set with μ'_1 ≥_Z μ and μ'_2 ≥_Z μ. Directedness gives uniqueness of a minimal element once one exists, but not existence. Both missing steps are standard: μ' = λ − λ' + NΣ_{α∈Δ}α^∨ is dominant and feasible for N large, which gives nonemptiness; and for a fixed feasible μ'_0 the dominant coweights μ with μ'_0 ≥_Z μ form a finite set, so a minimal element exists. sourceIssues.locator: §2.2, p. 5, the standing reduction, with §5.2, p. 9 and §5.4, pp. 10–11 (both versions)
sourceIssues.printed: As discussed in [GHN15, §2], the study of the nonemptiness pattern and dimension formula of affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties for an arbitrary reductive group may be reduced to simple and quasi-split groups over F. From now on, we assume that G is simple and quasi-split over F.
sourceIssues.correction: The reduction must also carry 'of adjoint type', as the cited section does: [GHN15, p. 648] reduces 'to the case where G is quasi-split and semisimple of adjoint type' (§2.2 Reduction to adjoint groups, §2.3, §2.4).
sourceIssues.reason: Adjointness is what makes §5 well defined. §5.2 introduces ρ^∨_J, the dominant coweight with ⟨ρ^∨_J, α_s⟩ = 1 for s ∈ J and 0 otherwise — that is, Σ_{s∈J} ω^∨_s — and §5.4 uses the elements w_1 = x z^{-1} t^{λ_w − ρ^∨_J} y' and w_2 = (y')^{-1} z t^{ρ^∨_J} y of W̃ and the element a t^γ of W̃. These require ρ^∨_J ∈ X_*(T)_{Γ_0}, which fails as soon as that lattice is smaller than the coweight lattice: for G = SL_3, split, X_*(T) is the coroot lattice of A_2, and y = s_1 gives J = {s_1} and ρ^∨_J = ω^∨_1 = (2α^∨_1 + α^∨_2)/3 ∉ X_*(T), so t^{ρ^∨_J} is not an element of W̃ at all. The twisted case shifts γ itself out of the lattice: in unramified simply connected ²A_2, with P^∨/Q^∨ = Z/3 and σ acting by −1, taking λ = 3ρ^∨, x = 1, y = s_1 gives J = {s_1}, σ^{-1}(ρ^∨_J) = ρ^∨_{σ^{-1}(J)} = ω^∨_2, and the class of γ in P^∨/Q^∨ is that of ω^∨_2 − ω^∨_1 ≠ 0, so no W_0-translate of it is a coweight of G. That this is a slip in summarising the reduction, and not a restriction the author intends, is clear from §1.2, which describes W̃ as 'the semidirect product of the coweight lattice with the relative Weyl group' — the coweight lattice being X_*(T) exactly for adjoint groups. Two consequences are worth recording: the cited reduction to adjoint groups holds under char k ∤ |π_1(G_ad)| and, after the authors' erratum, only component by component (see E13), and the descent of Theorem 6.1 from G_ad back to G is not written out.

sourceIssues.locator: §2.2, p. 5 (published version only; the sentence and the reference [BS17] are absent from arXiv:2001.03325)
sourceIssues.printed: In the equal characteristic, X_w(b) is the set of F̄_q-points of a scheme [BS17].
sourceIssues.correction: The cited result is about mixed characteristic: it gives X_w(b) as the F̄_q-points of a perfect scheme. In equal characteristic the affine flag variety is an ind-scheme by the classical construction, and no Witt vector geometry is needed.
sourceIssues.reason: [BS17] is Bhatt–Scholze, 'Projectivity of the Witt vector Grassmannian', whose subject is the Witt vector affine Grassmannian — W(k)-lattices in W(k)[1/p]^n — represented by an inductive limit of perfect schemes; it says nothing about equal characteristic, where the affine flag variety is an ind-scheme by Iwahori–Matsumoto, Bruhat–Tits and Faltings and X_w(b) is a locally closed subscheme of it. The sentence was added when the paper was revised: the arXiv version has neither it nor [BS17] in its bibliography, and states the scheme structure only in the notation of §5.3 ('locally closed sub-ind-schemes of the product of affine flag varieties').
